name: Adaptive music
oneLiner: Layered music that follows the game's state over F-03 chip music: each chip channel is a stem (bass, drums, melody, a tense danger line), drums come in for fights, the danger line at low health, the boss gets its own track. The game only reports active / combat / boss / hp each step; the module debounces flickers (0.5 s to start, 3 s to calm down, HP hysteresis), lands every change on the next bar line with a one-bar stinger when the mood changes, never overlaps two changes, and steps aside for the game's own jingles. Deterministic on the music clock, silent until the first click.
fits: top-down adventure and action RPG (exploring, fights, a boss room)
platformer and metroidvania with enemies and a boss
turn-based RPG with a field map and battle scenes
any game with chip music (F-03) and a hero with health
notFor: choosing tracks per scene only (title, field, battle): F-03 chip music alone does that
recorded audio stems or orchestral music

needs: one F-03 chip-music instance (shipped in the same basket; the game creates it once and steps it)
a per-step report read from game state: active (gameplay), combat (foes engaged or close), boss (a boss fight), hp (0-1)
the track picker that calls chip music's play() each step, returning null during gameplay
provides: layered music: update(report) every step, debounced, bar-quantized changes with stingers, no overlapping changes
state(): mood, low HP, layer gains, the pending change and when it lands, the hold left; plan(): every change with its bar line
gainsAt(clock) / curve() for visualizers, recent() events (commit, ignored, conflict), stats()

assets: module/adaptive-music.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_AdaptiveMusic) on top of F-03's public API: report handling with hysteresis, debounce, bar-quantized change planning, stingers, layer gains on chip music's channels, conflict detection, offline render for tests
original songs as chip-music pattern data in the module: two stem loops (Wildwood Trail, The Warden Wakes) and three one-bar stingers (Alarm, The Warden Rises, All Clear); no audio files
